# Appeal of Denial — Request for Reconsideration

**RE:** Appeal of adverse benefit determination
**Member:** Quinn Ellison
**Member ID:** W391580594
**Reference number:** POC-DF42BEB029-97975
**Date of denial notice:** August 4, 2026
**Service denied:** Partial knee replacement, CPT 27446
**Governing policy:** Aetna CPB 0660 – Knee Arthroplasty (https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/600_699/0660.html)

---

To the Appeals Department:

I am appealing the denial of coverage for a partial knee replacement (CPT 27446), which Aetna denied on August 4, 2026 under reference number POC-DF42BEB029-97975. The notice states that the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure. I am asking Aetna to reconsider that decision, because the imaging in my chart matches the imaging standard written into Aetna's own policy, Aetna CPB 0660 – Knee Arthroplasty, and my surgeon has documented that this procedure is needed.

Below I have set out the plan's published criteria and the matching documentation in my records.

## 1. The imaging criterion — the stated basis for the denial

The plan's policy states:

> "Radiographic evidence of moderate/severe osteoarthritis (i.e., Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 3 or 4) (see Appendix ) affecting only a single (medial, lateral or patellofemoral) compartment of the knee joint; and"

My records establish this. Imaging performed on May 28, 2026 (MRI of the knee) documents full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition, and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 medially. That is a Grade 4 finding, in a single compartment — the medial compartment — which is what this criterion asks for.

The policy also states:

> "Conservative therapy may be inappropriate for severe osteoarthritis with bone-on-bone articulation in the weight-bearing portion of the joint (medial and/or lateral but not patello-femoral); and"

My imaging documents bone-on-bone apposition in the medial compartment, which is the situation this sentence describes.

If Aetna's reviewer read the imaging differently, I respectfully ask that the plan identify, in writing, which part of the imaging criterion above it found was not met, and on what basis.

## 2. Pain and functional disability affecting daily activities

The plan's policy states:

> "Pain and functional disability that interferes with ADLs due to osteoarthritis or post-traumatic arthritis of the knee joint; and"

My records establish 18 months of progressive knee pain that is not relieved by rest. I cannot climb stairs without assistance, and I wake 3–4 times a night because of the pain.

## 3. Physical examination findings

The plan's policy states:

> "Limited range of motion, crepitus, or effusion or swelling of knee joint on physical examination: and"

My records document positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain.

I note that this criterion, as published, ends in a colon and introduces further material that I have not been given. The policy contains additional conditions that were not reproduced in the excerpts available to me. I ask Aetna to identify the specific criteria it applied in reaching this determination, so that I can respond to them directly.

## 4. Arc of motion

The plan's policy states:

> "Patient’s knee arc of motion (full extension to full flexion) is not limited to 90 degrees or less; and"

My records document that my range of motion is limited by pain, but they do not record a measurement in degrees. If a numeric measurement is required for this criterion, my surgeon's office can supply it: [measured arc of motion in degrees, from Dr. Lindqvist's office].

## 5. Conservative (non-surgical) treatment

The plan's policy states:

> "History of of unsuccessful conservative therapy (non-surgical medical management; 12 or 24 weeks depending on age/BMI) that is clearly addressed in the medical record (see Note Footnote3 *** ) with at least half of the necessary conservative therapy consisting of formal physical therapy (in-person with a licensed physical therapist as opposed to home or virtual physical therapy)."

My records establish the following:

- **Supervised, in-person physical therapy:** 16 weeks of supervised physical therapy focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, from February 25, 2026 to June 17, 2026, with 24 visits completed. This is documented in my physical therapy discharge note.
- **Anti-inflammatory medications or analgesics:** the policy lists *"Anti-inflammatory medications or analgesics; and"* — my records document NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief.
- **Flexibility and muscle strengthening exercises:** the policy lists *"Flexibility and muscle strengthening exercises; and"* — my physical therapy course was focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion.
- **Supervised physical therapy with diminished ADLs despite a plan of care:** the policy lists *"Supervised physical therapy (activities of daily living [ADLs] diminished despite completing a plan of care); and"* — I completed the full course of therapy and was discharged, and I still cannot climb stairs without assistance and still wake 3–4 times nightly with pain.
- **Therapeutic injections:** the policy states *"Therapeutic injections into the knee (required for persons with relative contraindications Footnote4 † to joint replacement, optional for others)."* I received a corticosteroid injection on May 2, 2026, which gave only 4 weeks of partial relief.

The policy describes the required duration as "12 or 24 weeks depending on age/BMI" but does not, in the language available to me, tell me which applies to my situation. My BMI is documented as 29 and my age is [my age]. I ask Aetna to state which duration it applied. My documented therapy consists of 16 weeks of in-person supervised physical therapy plus 8 months of NSAID treatment and an injection.

On the remaining items in this list — *"Activity modification; and"* and *"Assistive device use (required for persons with relative contraindications Footnote4 † to joint replacement, optional for others); and"* — the summary I have does not describe these separately. Additional documentation can be requested from my treating providers: [any activity modification and assistive device documentation from Dr. Lindqvist's office and my physical therapist].

The policy also states:

> "Physical therapy needs to be confirmed either by the actual PT notes, or by documentation in the member claims history."

My physical therapy is documented in the physical therapy discharge note, and the 24 visits between February 25, 2026 and June 17, 2026 should also appear in Aetna's own claims history. If the discharge note was not included in the material the reviewer saw, I ask that it be obtained and reviewed before a decision is made on this appeal.

## 6. Ligament stability, comorbidities, and HbA1c

The plan's policy states:

> "Member must have intact, stable ligaments, in particular the anterior cruciate ligament; and"

My records as summarized do not state a finding on ligament stability one way or the other. My surgeon can supply this: [ligament/ACL status from Dr. Lindqvist's examination and the MRI report of May 28, 2026].

The policy also states:

> "For members with significant conditions or co-morbidities, the risk/benefit of unicompartmental knee arthroplasty should be appropriately addressed in the medical record."

My records document no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker.

Finally, the policy states:

> "If member is diabetic, their hemoglobin A1C (HbA1c) should be less than 8 percent within 3 months prior to knee arthroplasty."

My records as submitted do not indicate that I am diabetic. If Aetna requires confirmation of this point, my provider can supply it: [diabetes status and, if applicable, most recent HbA1c].

## What I am asking for

I am asking Aetna to overturn the denial dated August 4, 2026 and authorize the partial knee replacement (CPT 27446) requested by my surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, MD, orthopedic surgery.

If Aetna maintains the denial, I ask that the plan provide, in writing:

1. the specific criterion or criteria from Aetna CPB 0660 – Knee Arthroplasty that it found were not met;
2. the reason the MRI of May 28, 2026 — documenting Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 with bone-on-bone apposition in the medial compartment only — was found not to satisfy the radiographic criterion quoted above; and
3. the credentials and specialty of the reviewer who made the determination.

I am also requesting a copy of all documents, records, and criteria the plan relied on in making this decision, and I ask that any records missing from the file — including my physical therapy discharge note and the MRI report — be obtained and reviewed.

My denial notice states that this appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice, by **January 31, 2027**. I am submitting this letter with Aetna's Member Complaint and Appeal Form (available in my account at aetna.com under complaints, grievances and appeals), sent to the appeal address printed on my denial notice. Aetna's published fax number for member appeals is 859-425-3379, and the member line is 1-800-872-3862 or the number on my card.

Thank you for reviewing this appeal.

Sincerely,

**Quinn Ellison**
Member ID: W391580594
Reference number: POC-DF42BEB029-97975
